raw_response:
I have been farming this land for fifty years. I know every corner of my 6 mu. My children go to work in town sometimes, so I cannot rely on much outside help — I have to plan around what I can manage with my own two hands and whoever is home.

**My thinking, crop by crop:**

**Cotton** — this is my main crop. I have grown cotton my whole life. The extension station gave me Bt hybrid cotton seed years ago and I kept buying it. It saves me some spraying on bollworm. I will plant 2 mu of cotton in late April. Cotton needs a lot of my attention but it brings cash. I will plough the plot deep before planting, apply base fertilizer, and top-dress at flowering. I know I need to irrigate at squaring, flowering, and boll-setting — that is 4 times with my well. Aphids and spider mites always come, so I will spray about 6 times across the season. I expect around 280 kg seed cotton per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Winter Wheat** — I plant wheat on 2 mu in October. I have done this so long I do it by feel. I use an improved certified variety from the county seed station — not fancy, but reliable on my soil. I plough and rotary till before sowing. Fertilizer base goes in at sowing, then I top-dress at jointing. I irrigate four times: the winter water before freezing, jointing, heading, and grain fill. Two or three pesticide applications — seed treatment plus an aphid and scab spray in spring. I expect about 400 kg per mu.

**Summer Maize** — right after wheat harvest in June, I plant maize on those same 2 mu. No time to rest the land. I use hybrid maize seed —郑单 (Zhengdan) type. I do rotary tillage after wheat straw, then sow quickly. Fertilizer all goes in as base since I am old and it is hot — hard to go back for top-dressing. I irrigate 3 times if summer is dry, less if we get rain. Fall armyworm has been a problem these past few years, so I spray 3 times now. I expect about 550 kg per mu.
